textbookText: PH3+ HBr→ PH4Br (phosphonium bromide) Note: PH3 is a weaker base than NH3. 3. Action with Cl2 Depending upon the reaction condition phosphine reacts with chlorine to give phosphorous trichloride or phosphorous pentachloride.

PH3 +3Cl2 → PCl3 (phosphorous trichloride) PH3+ 4Cl2→ PCl5 + HCl (phosphorous pentachloride) 4. Reducing Nature Phosphine acts as a reducing agent. For example, a) Phosphine reduces silver nitrate solution to metallic silver. PH3+ AgNO3 + 3H2O→ 6Ag↓ + 6HNO3 + H3PO3
b) Phosphine reduces copper sulphate to black ppt. of copper phosphide. PH3+ 3CuSO4→ Cu3P2↓ + 3H2SO4
c) Phosphine reduces mercuric chloride to black ppt. of mercuric phosphide. PH3+ 3HgCl2→ Hg3P2↓ + 6HCl
a. How would you confirm that PH3 is a reducing agent? b. How does phosphine react with chlorine gas?

Uses of phosphine Some of the applications of phosphine gas are listed below: a. It is used as a reducing agent. b. It is used in preparation of smoke screens which are used in warfare. c. It is used to prepare various compounds of phosphorous like P2O5, PCl3, PCl5, etc. d. It is used as a Holme's signal to guide the ship.
